summary.headline: Alicon Castalloy Q2 FY27 total income hit a record ₹652 crore, up 50.4% YoY, while consolidated EBITDA margin stayed near 10%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income of ₹652 crore was the highest ever for a single quarter, up 50.4% YoY and 12.6% QoQ, with management citing alloy price pass-through as part of the growth. Consolidated EBITDA rose 14% YoY to ₹65.3 crore, but margin of 10% (12.1% adjusted for aluminium prices) was held back by commodity and energy inflation. H1 FY27 total income was ₹1,231 crore (+44% YoY), with H1 EBITDA margin at 9.8%. Management reiterated FY27 alloy-adjusted revenue growth guidance of 10-15%, and said the order book stood at about ₹6,700 crore as of 30 September.

financial_highlights.value: ~₹70 crore including ~₹40 crore leasing; FY27 plan ~₹150 crore

segments.name: Domestic automotive
segments.commentary: Domestic business grew ahead of market; industry growth ~19% YoY in Q2 versus Alicon's 24% alloy-adjusted growth. Segment mix (H1): two-wheelers ~40%, passenger vehicles ~36-38%, commercial vehicles ~18%, rest non-auto.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Cylinder-head share of Indian CV business rose from ~30% in FY26 to 23% in H1 FY27, with further gains expected by year-end. Management said CV volumes grew around 10% additionally in the quarter from programmes completed in FY26.

segments.name: International (Europe, Slovakia)
segments.commentary: International revenue share was ~13% in Q2; sequential growth was registered as mature programmes ended. Management expects the share to reach ~18-20% by end-FY27. A new German OEM business was won for the Slovakia plant.

segments.name: Non-automotive
segments.commentary: Non-auto is ~5% of order wins; data-centre parts go into SOP in March 2027 with ~₹15-20 crore expected next year. A tractor integrated cylinder head and air intake manifold programme targets SOP in about five months, with ~₹12-15 crore a year expected.

guidance_outlook: FY27 alloy-adjusted revenue growth guided at 10-15%; management said it could be higher, but Q3 is seasonally soft and Q4 is strong.
FY27 tonnage growth expected at around 15% or more.
EBITDA margin expected to reach about 12% in FY27 on an alloy-adjusted basis, with ~1 percentage point improvement a year thereafter and 14-15% targeted by FY30.
Aluminium prices expected to fall ~20-25% from September to December 2026; management said raw-material inflation has been passed through to customers in full, with a time lag on receipts.
Profit before tax at the European subsidiary expected to turn positive next year; European break-even estimated at ~₹30-40 crore quarterly sales.
New Pune plant (12,000 MT capacity, ~₹125-130 crore investment) expected to start mass manufacturing by April 2027; first-year revenue ~₹120-150 crore, with peak asset turnover of ~3x.

Order book of ~₹6,700 crore as of 30 September, covering FY27 to FY32 period. Q2 wins: eight parts from three customers, ~₹270 crore peak annual sales, ~₹1,000 crore over six years, mostly from FY28-29.
capex_capacity: Current capacity ~50,000 tonnes a year; utilisation ~82-84%, with management preferring 84-85% as the ideal level.
New Pune plant adds 12,000 tonnes a year; mass manufacturing targeted by April 2027.
FY27 capex plan ~₹150 crore including the Pune plant; H1 capex ~₹70 crore, of which ~₹40 crore was leased; funded primarily through internal accruals.
Additional strategic capacity under evaluation; management said no further plant announcement yet and that inorganic options will be shared once mature.
Cylinder-head market share estimates: two-wheelers ~30-35%, passenger vehicles ~14-18%, commercial vehicles ~13-15% (25-28% of the aluminium addressable market).
demand_pricing: Aluminium is the main raw material; alloy price increases inflated reported revenue. Management said the main growth drivers are volume, richer mix and new programmes.
Value addition rose 30.4% QoQ and 22% YoY; management is shifting the mix towards higher-VA and complex parts.
Commodity, energy and labour inflation, plus the war-related cost pressures, constrained margin; management is working on price recovery and productivity.
Global castings shortage noted; machine lead times have risen by one to two months, but management sees no significant constraint.
Europe: inflation in manpower and power is pressuring peers; management said European cost base was cut by more than 50% in recent years.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the three Q2 order wins: lifetime value, timing and near-term SOPs?
qa_highlights.answer: Eight parts from three customers, ~95% passenger vehicles and ~5% non-auto; ~₹270 crore peak annual sales and ~₹1,000 crore over six years, mostly from FY28-29. 25-30 new part numbers to go into SOP over the next year, including global AV and commercial programmes.

qa_highlights.question: Expected export share of revenue and the revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Export share ~13% in Q2, expected at 18-20% by end-FY27, rising a further ~3% in subsequent years. H1 mix: two-wheelers ~40%, PV ~36-38%, CV ~18%, rest non-auto; EV ~4-5% and hybrids ~6-7% of revenue; machining share ~68%.

qa_highlights.question: What drove 19% volume growth and is the FY27 revenue guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from CV programmes that completed in FY26, higher share of business with existing customers, and deemed exports via two Chennai-based customers. Management is looking at 15% or more alloy-adjusted growth and is guiding 10-15% for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for aluminium prices and the margin path to FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium expected to fall 20-25% from September to December 2026. Margin guided to ~12% this year on an alloy-adjusted basis, 14-15% by FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why keep investing in the European plant and what is the viability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says Slovakia has lower inflation than Western Europe, niche high-tech work is hard to offshore, and new enquiries are rising. European PAT loss of ~₹3 crore a quarter is expected to turn positive next year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and inventory rise and what does it mean for cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to volume growth and higher aluminium prices, plus customer approval cycles; collections are expected in the next two to three months. Management said the lag affects cash only, not margins.

qa_highlights.question: Cylinder-head market share and captive production?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said OEMs are offloading cylinder-head production to vendors; the largest customer makes ~85% in-house. Management expects share to rise over time.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on aluminium price declines and pass-through timing; H1 EBITDA margin was 9.8% against 12.7% a year earlier.
Working capital: receivables rose ~₹88 crore and inventory ~₹32 crore in Q2, weighing on cash conversion; 34 working-capital days.
European subsidiary is loss-making (~₹3 crore a quarter at PAT level); legacy programme losses and the break-even threshold need to be watched.
Q3 is seasonally weak; Q4 must deliver for FY27 guidance. Management said it is cautious on demand volatility.
Pune plant mass-production timing (April 2027) and ramp-up; asset turnover target of ~3x.
Management declined to give a numeric target beyond FY27 export and revenue targets; a strategic plan is due to be shared later.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, order wins and the domestic CV and hybrid programmes, but cautious on margins, cash conversion and the external demand outlook. Management was reluctant to give hard numbers on post-FY27 targets, and some answers on the European business were qualitative.
key_quotes: We reported total income of 652 crore, which is the highest ever in a single quarter.
We are more focused on higher displacement platforms, more complex applications and products that offer better value addition.
Our objective is not simply to increase production volumes. We want to generate greater value from the manufacturing infrastructure and capital already employed.
We expect to move into mass manufacturing by April 2027 as submitted before.

growth.why: FY27 alloy-adjusted revenue growth guided at 12-15% (midpoint 12.5%, management says could be higher), backed by the new 12,000 t Pune plant due for mass manufacturing by April 2027, a ~₹6,700 crore order book, and a richer mix; utilisation ~83% of 50k t capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides ~12% alloy-adjusted EBITDA margin in FY27 (Q2 was 10.0%, 12.1% adjusted), ~1pp a year after, to 14-15% by FY30, with aluminium expected to fall 20-25% from September to December 2026.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: New 12,000 t/yr Pune plant (~24% of current 50,000 t capacity) is under construction with mass manufacturing targeted by April 2027, and first-year revenue is pegged at ~₹120-150 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Tonnage grew 19.3% YoY in Q2 and management expects FY27 tonnage growth of around 15% or more, backed by CV programmes, 25-30 new part numbers entering SOP over the next year and the Q2 order wins (~₹270 crore peak annual sales).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is ~82-84% against management's preferred 84-85%, and additional strategic capacity is under evaluation, but management said no further plant announcement yet and inorganic options will be shared once mature.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 alloy-adjusted revenue growth 'could be higher' than the 10-15% guided range and is looking at 15% or more, but Q3 is seasonally soft and Q4 has to deliver.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin was 9.8% against 12.7% a year earlier, and management is cautious on demand volatility, commodity/energy/labour inflation and the war-related cost pressures; Q3 is seasonally weak.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Data-centre parts go into SOP in March 2027 (~₹15-20 crore expected next year), a tractor integrated cylinder head and air intake manifold programme targets SOP in about five months (~₹12-15 crore a year), and 25-30 new part numbers enter SOP over the next year.

rows.label: Q2 FY27 order wins ~₹1,000 crore lifetime value
rows.why: Eight parts from three customers with ~₹270 crore peak annual sales and ~₹1,000 crore over six years, mostly ramping in FY28-29, on a ~₹6,700 crore order book.

rows.label: European subsidiary break-even and turn to profit
rows.why: European PAT loss of ~₹3 crore a quarter is expected to turn positive next year, with break-even at ~₹30-40 crore quarterly sales; a new German OEM business was won for the Slovakia plant and international share is expected to rise from ~13% to 18-20% by end-FY27.

rows.label: Receivables and inventory unwind
rows.why: Receivables rose ~₹88 crore and inventory ~₹32 crore in Q2 (34 working-capital days), and management expects collections in the next two to three months, so cash conversion should improve.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, the Q2 order wins, CV share gains and the Pune plant timing, but cautious on margins, cash conversion and external demand; analysts pressed on European viability, receivables build-up and post-FY27 targets, which management answered qualitatively.
